articles.body: Decoding LLM Inference Economics: Real-World TTFT & Throughput Benchmarks Across Hosted APIs When architecting production LLM systems, engineers spend weeks fine-tuning prompts, evaluating embedding strategies, and optimizing RAG pipelines. Yet, many treat the hosted inference endpoint as a black-box utility: you send an HTTP POST request, and tokens trickle back. This abstraction is dangerous. Recent empirical data from NeuBench speed testing reveals token throughput variances of up to 40% across major hosted LLM providers for the exact same model weights.

articles.body: Originally published on kuryzhev.cloud The scenario: a Friday-evening exploit report It is 18:40 on a Friday. A customer emails your two-person team a proof-of-concept for your firmware update daemon, with a link to a forum thread where someone is already using it. Before September 2026 that was a bad evening. Now it also starts a legal clock, because CRA vulnerability reporting has been mandatory since 11 Sep 2026. For actively exploited vulnerabilities, manufacturers of products with digital elements must send an early warning within 24 hours and a fuller notification within 72 hours. The Commission's overview is at digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cra-reporting . Large companies have legal and compliance staff for this. Small teams have whoever is on call.

articles.title: Linux file Descriptor Limits and Socket Leaks: ulimit and /proc/sys/fs/file-max
articles.excerpt: Originally published on Code Beneath. Understanding Linux File Descriptors and the ulimit System Per-process soft and hard limits: controlled by ulimit -n and configured in /etc/security/limits.conf.…
articles.body: Originally published on Code Beneath . You deploy a service, it runs fine for hours, then crashes with "too many open files." The root cause is almost always a file descriptor socket leak, triggered by improper cleanup or hitting the system ulimit. Understanding the two-tier limit system (per-process and system-wide), how to detect leaks, and how to configure both layers properly is essential for any engineer running network services. This article shows you the exact mechanisms, monitoring commands, and working code to diagnose and fix descriptor exhaustion in production. Understanding Linux File Descriptors and the ulimit System Every open file, socket, pipe, and device in Linux is represented by a file descriptor (FD), a small integer starting at 0.

articles.title: AI Security Starts at the System Boundary: Threat-Modelling the Full LLM Application
articles.excerpt: An AI model is not the whole AI system. A deployed large-language-model application may combine a model, prompts, user input, retrieval systems, APIs, identity controls, logs and downstream actions. S…
articles.body: An AI model is not the whole AI system. A deployed large-language-model application may combine a model, prompts, user input, retrieval systems, APIs, identity controls, logs and downstream actions. Security failures can occur at the boundaries between these components—even when the model itself behaves as designed. That distinction matters because “the model gave an unexpected answer” is not a complete threat model. The engineering question is broader: What data can enter the system, what can the system access, and what actions can it take?

articles.title: Stream Telegram Media Uploads in PHP via cURL to Avoid Out-of-Memory Crashes
articles.excerpt: Automating PDF invoice generation, daily data exports, or user media delivery through Telegram bots in PHP looks simple on paper. However, naive implementations frequently crash in production. Develop…
articles.body: Automating PDF invoice generation, daily data exports, or user media delivery through Telegram bots in PHP looks simple on paper. However, naive implementations frequently crash in production. Developers often attempt to read whole files into string buffers using file_get_contents() or pass arbitrary remote URLs to Telegram's API without size validation. When your background worker attempts to send a 40MB export file on a server configured with a standard 128MB memory_limit , the script runs out of RAM, leaving the queue stalled and the user hanging without feedback. Even when files do send successfully, re-uploading the exact same binary payload across hundreds of users burns server outbound bandwidth and triggers rate limits ( 429 Too Many Requests ).
articles.author: Serhii

articles.title: How do you reduce hallucination?
articles.excerpt: Asked in an AI engineer interview. What they are really testing: whether you treat hallucination as a system-level problem with layered controls (grounding, retrieval quality, prompting, verification,…
articles.body: Asked in an AI engineer interview. What they are really testing: whether you treat hallucination as a system-level problem with layered controls (grounding, retrieval quality, prompting, verification, and evaluation), rather than one trick like "lower the temperature." A strong answer: Ground the model: use RAG so answers come from retrieved passages, and instruct the model to answer only from context and to say "I don't know" when the context is insufficient. Fix retrieval first: most RAG hallucinations are retrieval failures. Tune chunking, use hybrid search (BM25 plus dense vectors), add a reranker, and tune top-k so the context is relevant without flooding the window.

articles.title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
articles.excerpt: Certain configurations of Alpine are affected. Other distros may be as well.
articles.body: Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password. The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations.

Or, if you just want to watch your pre-load complete incredibly quickly, this is also an option. You can click here to learn more about how to activate this offer if you're a Spectrum user. articles.title: 'We got it done!' Spacewalking astronauts finish installing next-gen ISS solar arrays
articles.excerpt: Spacewalkers Anil Menon and Joshua Kutryk installed the final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array on Thursday (Nov. 5), wrapping up a multiyear effort to boost the station's power generation by 30%.
articles.body: Just as NASA is preparing to demonstrate " Max Power " on the ground, two astronauts on a spacewalk have provided the International Space Station (ISS) with the same. Expedition 75 flight engineers Anil Menon of NASA and Joshua Kutryk of the Canadian Space Agency installed and deployed the eighth and final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) on Thursday (Nov. 5), augmenting the space station's legacy solar array wings to produce as much as 30% more electricity. "We got it done!" said Menon at the end of the 6-hour-and-59-minute spacewalk . The EVA (extravehicular activity) began at 8:36 a.m. EST and ended at 3:35 p.m. EST (1336 to 2035 GMT).

articles.title: Andy Weir says his new sci-fi audio drama 'Exoplanet' is a way to 'revive the old art of radio plays' (interview)
articles.excerpt: "Earlier on in my life, even before 'The Martian,' I wanted to bring back audio-only entertainment."
articles.body: Hot off the tremendous theatrical success of this year's "Project Hail Mary," adapted from Andy Weir's 2021 novel of the same name, the New York Times bestselling author is rocketing back into deep space with a brand new Audible Original release landing on Nov. 5, 2026, titled " Exoplanet ." Weir (" The Martian ") is executive producing this ambitious full-cast audiobook drama with acclaimed author and ace comic writer Benjamin Percy ("Wolverine") for the first in a series of curated sci-fi projects for Amazon's Audible. The seven-episode sci-fi thriller stars the vocal talents of Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo in a wild time-travel space disaster odyssey that also benefits from Lucasfilm’s Skywalker Sound, which provided the show’s immersive acoustic elements.

articles.title: Blue Origin announces 3rd stage for its powerful New Glenn rocket —and a new engine
articles.excerpt: Blue Origin has developed a third stage for its New Glenn rocket, which it says will make the launcher even more flexible and capable. The company has also built a new engine, called Northstar.
articles.body: Blue Origin's big rocket is getting a little bigger. Jeff Bezos' company announced today (Nov. 5) that it has developed a third stage for its New Glenn rocket, which it says will make the powerful launcher more capable and flexible. The stage, called the GS3, "enhances New Glenn's capabilities," Blue Origin said in a blog post today . "The third stage enables direct deployment of satellite constellations to GEO [ geostationary orbit ] and supports heavy-lift science and exploration missions to the moon and deep space." Illustration of the variants of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, with the new GS3 third stage now in the mix. (Image credit: Blue Origin) New Glenn is a two-stage vehicle at the moment.
